The index MongoDB creates for you
Every collection is born with _id_
lecture7> db.students.getIndexes() [   { v: 2,     key: { _id: 1 },     name: "_id_" } ]
Unique — no two documents can share an _id
Fast lookup — findOne({ _id: … }) never scans
Can't be dropped — replication and updates rely on it
Every other field — age, email, city — has no index until you create one.
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Remember "Indexes 1" in the Atlas screenshot (Lecture 2)? This was it.

The one rule to remember
Examined should ≈ returned
age 20 · no index
10 / 30
age 20 · index age_1
10 / 10
email · no index
1 / 50,000
email · unique index
1 / 1
Bar = useful reads. Full bar = every document read was part of the answer.
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · nReturned / totalDocsExamined — the closer to 1, the better

MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Like a phone book: sorted by surname, then first name — useless for finding first names alone
Covered query · the best case
Answer from the index alone
db.students.createIndex({ grade: 1, name: 1 }) db.students.find({ grade: "A" }, { _id: 0, grade: 1, name: 1 })
totalKeysExamined
12
totalDocsExamined

Everything asked for is already in the index → no documents fetched
Plan shows IXSCAN, no FETCH
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Must hide _id (it isn't in this index) · if another index wins, add .hint("grade_1_name_1")
Unique index · use case: roll numbers, emails, usernames
Speed + a guard against duplicates
db.students.createIndex(   { roll: 1 }, { unique: true })
Created — all 30 rolls differ
Now inserting a second "A001" is refused.
db.students.createIndex(   { mobile: 1 }, { unique: true })
E11000 duplicate key
"9876543210" is shared by Aditi, Kavya and Uday — clean data first.
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · The _id_ index you got for free is a unique index too
TTL index · use case: OTPs, login sessions, logs
Documents that delete themselves
db.otps.createIndex({ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 60 }) db.otps.insertOne({ phone: "9876543210", otp: 4821, createdAt: new Date() })
0 s
OTP saved, user gets an SMS
60 s
OTP has expired
≈ 60–120 s
background job removes it — find() returns [ ]
Rule: the field must hold a real Date. A string like "2025-01-05" never expires.
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Worksheet example: logs with expireAfterSeconds: 3600 = auto-delete after 1 hour
Summary
Six index types, six real jobs
Type
How to create
Real-life job
Single
{ age: 1 }
filter students by age
Compound
{ grade: 1, age: 1 }
filter on two fields
Unique
{ email: 1 }, { unique: true }
one account per email
TTL
{ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 60 }
OTPs, sessions
Multikey
{ tags: 1 } on an array field
products by tag (automatic)
Text
{ title: "text" }
search bar on words
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Created automatically: only _id_ (and the shard-key index when you shard)
The price of an index
Faster reads, slower writes
insertOne()
collection
_id_
age_1
email_1
1 insert = 4 writes. Every index also uses disk and RAM.
Do index fields you filter or sort on often
Don't index every field "just in case"
Drop indexes no query uses
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Read-heavy apps (shops, catalogs) gain most · write-heavy logs need fewer indexes
Managing indexes
List, drop, clean up
db.students.getIndexes()
see every index and its name
db.students.dropIndex("age_1")
remove one index, by name
db.students.dropIndexes()
remove all — _id_ always stays
.explain("executionStats")
prove an index is actually used
In Compass: collection → Indexes tab to create or drop · Explain button for the plan
MongoDB Series · Lecture 07 · Worksheet fix: use dropIndex("age_1") for one index; dropIndexes() removes all non-_id indexes
The big picture · indexes in a sharded cluster
Indexes work on every machine
1
mongos uses the shard key to pick the right machine
2
Each mongod keeps its own indexes for its own data
3
The shard key must have an index
No shard key in the query → asks all 3 machines. No index → each one does a COLLSCAN.
